issues.detail: The Hebrew mentions 'for the golden bowls by weight for each bowl and bowl' (לִכְפוֹרֵ֨י הַזָּהָ֤ב בְּמִשְׁקָל֙ לִכְפ֣וֹר וּכְפ֔וֹר) and 'for the silver bowls by weight for each bowl and bowl' (וְלִכְפוֹרֵ֥י הַכֶּ֛סֶף בְּמִשְׁקָ֖ל לִכְפ֥וֹר וּכְפֽוֹר). The Chinese renders '每個金碗按重量，每個銀碗也按重量' which captures the idea of each bowl by weight, but the Hebrew explicitly distinguishes 'golden bowls' (לִכְפוֹרֵי הַזָּהָב) and 'silver bowls' (לִכְפוֹרֵי הַכֶּסֶף) as separate categories. The Chinese says '金碗' and '銀碗' which is correct. However, the Hebrew also includes 'the forks, basins, and pitchers' (הַמִּזְלָגוֹת וְהַמִּזְרָקוֹת וְהַקְּשָׂוֹת) made of pure gold, and the Chinese says '純金叉子、盆子和壺' which is correct. The issue is that the Hebrew phrase 'וְלִכְפוֹרֵי הַזָּהָב בְּמִשְׁקָל לִכְפוֹר וּכְפוֹר' and 'וְלִכְפוֹרֵי הַכֶּסֶף בְּמִשְׁקָל לִכְפוֹר וּכְפוֹר' uses the distributive 'לִכְפוֹר וּכְפוֹר' (for each bowl and bowl) which the Chinese renders as '每個' (each), which is acceptable. The main potential omission is that the Hebrew says 'golden bowls' and 'silver bowls' separately, but the Chinese says '金碗' and '銀碗' which is fine. However, the Chinese adds '定了' (determined/set) which is not in the Hebrew; the Hebrew simply lists items with 'and' (וְ). The Hebrew has no verb 'determined' or 'set'; it is a list of items with their weights. The Chinese '又定了' (also determined) introduces a verb not present in the Hebrew, which could be an addition. But the context (1 Chronicles 28) may imply weighing, but the Hebrew text here is a list. The Chinese also says '重量' (weight) which corresponds to 'בְּמִשְׁקָל' (by weight). The main issue is the addition of '定了' (determined) which is not in the Hebrew, and the omission of the explicit 'pure gold' for the bowls? Actually the Hebrew says 'זָהָב טָהוֹר' (pure gold) for the forks, basins, and pitchers, but the bowls are described as 'golden bowls' and 'silver bowls' without specifying purity. The Chinese says '純金叉子、盆子和壺' which is correct. The Chinese says '每個金碗按重量，每個銀碗也按重量' which is correct. The addition of '定了' is a minor addition but does not change the meaning significantly. However, the Hebrew has no verb, so adding '定了' is an addition. But the instruction says to flag only if a Chinese reader would believe something factually different. The addition of '定了' (determined) might imply that David determined the weights, which is not in the text but could be inferred from context. However, the Hebrew is a list of items with their weights, not a statement of determination. This could be considered an addition. But the main issue is that the Chinese omits the explicit 'golden' and 'silver' distinction? No, it has them. Actually, the Chinese says '金碗' and '銀碗' which is correct. The Hebrew has 'לִכְפוֹרֵי הַזָּהָב' (for the golden bowls) and 'לִכְפוֹרֵי הַכֶּסֶף' (for the silver bowls). The Chinese says '金碗' and '銀碗' which is correct. The issue is the addition of '定了' (determined) which is not in the Hebrew. Also, the Hebrew has 'וְהַמִּזְלָגוֹת וְהַמִּזְרָקוֹת וְהַקְּשָׂוֹת זָהָב טָהוֹר' (and the forks and the basins and the pitchers of pure gold) – the Chinese says '純金叉子、盆子和壺' which is correct. The Chinese adds '的重量' (the weight of) which is not in the Hebrew for the first list; the Hebrew just says 'of pure gold' without mentioning weight for the forks, basins, pitchers. The Chinese says '又定了純金叉子、盆子和壺的重量' which adds '重量' (weight) for the first list, but the Hebrew only mentions weight for the bowls. This is an addition. The Hebrew says 'וְהַמִּזְלָגוֹת וְהַמִּזְרָקוֹת וְהַקְּשָׂוֹת זָהָב טָהוֹר' – no mention of weight. The Chinese says '又定了純金叉子、盆子和壺的重量' – adds '重量' (weight) for these items. That is an addition. Also, the Hebrew has 'וְלִכְפוֹרֵי הַזָּהָב בְּמִשְׁקָל' – 'and for the golden bowls by weight' – the Chinese says '每個金碗按重量' which is correct. The addition of '重量' for the first list is a factual addition. So flag for addition. Also, the Chinese says '又定了' which is an addition of a verb. So overall, flag for addition of '重量' for the forks, basins, pitchers, and the verb '定了'.
